clue.text: One who lodges, say, at the frontier

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the words spoken, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: a lodger in someone's house is a boarder

explanation.surface: A lodger lives right on the national boundary line.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the edge or boundary line between two countries, the same as a frontier.

clue.text: La belle Helene, say, in top rate English version

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Offenbach's work staged in a premium-priced English production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' signals rearranging TOPRATE plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: La Belle Helene is a comic light opera by Offenbach, an example of that musical genre.

clue.text: Condescended to accept lass at last as intended

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to condescend is to deign, so condescended gives deigned

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word lass

explanation.surface: Someone stooped to welcome a girl, just as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designed was planned on purpose, meaning it was intended.

clue.text: Doubly concerned with black eye, going to bat

indicators.note: doubly says the next piece is used twice over in a row

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
mouse is slang for a bruised black eye

explanation.surface: Someone with a shiner is twice as bothered about getting hit with a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' is a link. REREMOUSE is an archaic word for the flying mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reremouse is an old dialect name for the flying mammal, the bat.

clue.text: Glad need ran out for this old tax

indicators.note: ran out suggests the letters scattering loose and reforming in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone happy about a need that was used up for some ancient levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran out' rearranges GLADNEED; 'for this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danegeld was a land tax raised in Anglo-Saxon England to buy off Viking raiders.

clue.text: In every respect it's the responsibility of the Oval, for example

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning completely, thoroughly, through and through

definitions.text: the responsibility of the Oval, for example
definitions.meaning: the Oval is a London cricket ground, so a thing left to such a venue is its duty

explanation.surface: Something is entirely the job of a famous cricket venue.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; the phrase read literally means a matter left to a ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom suits someone perfectly or completely, so it means in every respect.

clue.text: Formerly a Treasury question

parts.note: ex is the prefix meaning former or formerly
a mine is a rich store or treasury, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: An enquiry once put to the government's finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasury' looks like the government office but is a mine, a rich store.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone is to question or interrogate them closely.

clue.text: Sort of polystyrene spread out

definitions.meaning: a light foamed packing material is called by this name
enlarged or extended over a wider area

explanation.surface: A packaging foam laid across the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Expanded polystyrene is the foamed packing form; something expanded has also been spread out.

clue.text: Extremely desirable widow's neglected

indicators.note: extremely points at the extreme letters of desirable, its first and last

parts.note: relict is an archaic word for a widow, one left behind

explanation.surface: A very attractive widow has been ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier but takes the first and last letters of 'desirable', D and E; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Derelict property has been abandoned and left uncared for, so neglected.

clue.text: Group warder has fastener that prevents movement

parts.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
screw is British slang for a prison officer

explanation.surface: A team of prison guards owns a locking device.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is British slang for a prison warder.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew is a small screw that holds a part fixed in place so it cannot shift.

clue.text: One puffing a cigarette

definitions.meaning: someone breathless and panting for air
an old British slang name for a cheap cigarette

explanation.surface: A smoker drawing on a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gasps is breathing hard, and gasper is also old British slang for a cheap cigarette.

clue.text: Cat gets a bird, almost back in tree

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled run is read from the end to the start

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A cat catches a bird and nearly gets back up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the bird's last letter, and 'back' turns the whole run around; 'gets' and 'in' are links. The surface cat climbing a tree is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a citrus tree whose fruit gives the oil that flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Memorable gesture

definitions.meaning: notable or outstanding, as in a notable victory
a sign or motion made to communicate

explanation.surface: An unforgettable wave of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal victory is a striking, memorable one, and a signal is also a gesture conveying a message.

clue.text: Like a gathering, liable to break out

definitions.meaning: a gathering here is a boil or pus-filled swelling that bursts through the skin
likely to burst forth violently, like a volcano

explanation.surface: A crowd that may turn riotous at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like a crowd but is a medical term for a boil or abscess.
explanation.definitionFit: Eruptive describes something bursting out, such as a boil or a volcano.

clue.text: One with dual visa badly needs help to make things clear

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are messed up and set in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller with two visas is in a muddle and needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I plus DUALVISA; 'with' and 'needs' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual aid is a chart or picture used to help explain something clearly.

clue.text: Smooth sort of man to put children out

definitions.meaning: to rub a surface down until it is level and even

definitions.text: sort of man to put children out
definitions.meaning: the sleep-bringing figure of folklore is a sandman, who sends children to sleep

explanation.surface: A suave fellow knocking children unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' means send to sleep, not knock out: the folklore Sandman sends children to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand wood is to smooth it, and sand gives the folklore figure who brings sleep.

clue.text: Keep one's distance as man has to undress

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, short for Stanley
to doff is to take off clothing

explanation.surface: Someone stays back while a man has to strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand off is to stay away or remain aloof, keeping at a distance.

clue.text: Can you make one tin do for lunchtime? Certainly

indicators.note: to make something out of these words means building a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Can you stretch one tin of food to feed everyone at midday?
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges ONETINDO; 'Can you' and 'Certainly' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is a literary word for midday, the usual time for lunch.

clue.text: Means of access to mine diamonds in island

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in cards

explanation.surface: Diamonds lie on an island, reached through a mineshaft.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT (or eyot) is a small island in a river, such as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage driven into a hillside to reach a mine.

clue.text: Promote barman

definitions.meaning: to support or argue in favour of
a member of the bar, a lawyer who pleads cases in court

explanation.surface: Give a pub worker a step up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' looks like a pub worker but means a lawyer called to the Bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to promote it, and an advocate is a barrister who pleads in court.

clue.text: I'm having nothing to do, love, with this pansy

definitions.meaning: the state of being unoccupied or without work
love-in-... is an old folk name for the wild pansy, so love joined to this word names the flower

explanation.surface: Someone tells their partner they're bored, holding a pansy.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-idleness, the wild pansy, appears in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of being unoccupied, having nothing to do.

clue.text: Relieved from pain after a month, and departed

indicators.note: after says the first-named piece comes after the second

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December
eased means made less painful

explanation.surface: Someone's suffering lifted after a month, and then they died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' is a euphemism for dead; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The departed are the dead, so deceased means the same as departed.

clue.text: Heart stimulant is extracted with the fingers

indicators.note: is extracted says the letters of is are taken out of the drug name

parts.note: digitalis is a drug from foxglove used to strengthen the heartbeat

explanation.surface: A cardiac drug is drawn out of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital means relating to the fingers or digits, so done with the fingers.

clue.text: State of being unable to marry girl, for example, on the rebound

definitions.text: State of being unable to marry

parts.note: Nona is a girl's name

indicators.note: on the rebound means bounced back, so the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A jilted girl is now on the rebound and can't wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is legal minority, being too young to marry without consent.

clue.text: Worked out number erased by mistake

indicators.note: by mistake hints the letters are set down wrongly, in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A figure was rubbed out in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' rearranges NO plus ERASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoned means thought through logically, as worked out.

clue.text: Does it ease pain of operation, I worried?

parts.note: taken as written
ate means troubled, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether the drug will relieve pain after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug that dulls pain, so it is the thing asked about.

clue.text: Great bed place girl's grabbed unexpectedly

indicators.note: grabbed means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Una is a girl's name; the possessive gives the final S
the Great Bed of Ware is a famous huge bed from the Hertfordshire town of Ware

explanation.surface: A girl seizes a large bed by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: WARE is a Hertfordshire town, home of the Great Bed of Ware, now in the V&A museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught unawares means taken by surprise, so unexpectedly.

clue.text: Sponge in complementary pack

parts.note: free means given at no charge, as complimentary is
a load is a pack or burden carried

explanation.surface: A bath sponge comes in a matching set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complementary' stands for complimentary, given free.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others without paying, which is to freeload.

clue.text: Elaborate squirrel's nest containing mosses in the middle

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a drey is the nest of a squirrel

indicators.note: in the middle points to the central letters of mosses

explanation.surface: A squirrel's nest lined with moss.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of MOSSES is SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate clothing is showy and fancy, which is dressy.
